DU preset validation mismatch:
Issue: The Dispensing Unit (DU) preset logic fails to match the authorized transaction amount.
Check 1: Reboot the DU controller board by flipping breaker #3 in the electrical panel.
Check 2: If the issue persists, inspect the RS485 communication cable between the DU and the forecourt controller for loose connections or corrosion.
Check 3: Recalibrate the pulse meter logic. Spare parts needed: 1x Pulse Meter Unit (Part #PM-400), 1x Serial Connector.
ATG communication failure:
Issue: The Automatic Tank Gauge (ATG) is failing to transmit stock data to the controller.
Check 1: Verify that the physical connection at the tank probe head is securely fastened and free of water ingress.
Check 2: Check the intrinsic safety barrier inside the station building for blown fuses.
Check 3: Reset the ATG console. If the probe still fails, replace the sensor head. Spare parts needed: 1x ATG Probe Head (Part #AT-99), 1x Intrinsic Fuse (100mA).
Possible tank leak, flagged by ATG:
Issue: The tank stock variance has exceeded safe environmental limits.
Check 1: IMMEDIATELY halt all dispensing from the affected tank via the forecourt controller.
Check 2: Perform a manual dip test using water finding paste to rule out sudden water ingress.
Check 3: Visually inspect the shear valve and sump area for pooling fuel. Deploy the Hazmat team if pooling is confirmed. No immediate spare parts; priority is containment.
Likely PSP/battery-related power issue (:
Issue: The predictive model indicates an impending UPS battery failure due to voltage drop.
Check 1: Navigate to the UPS room and check the LCD panel for 'Battery End of Life' warnings.
Check 2: Use a multimeter to measure the DC float voltage across the battery banks (should be ~13.5V per block).
Check 3: If voltage is below 12.0V during charge cycle, the battery blocks must be replaced. Spare parts needed: 4x 12V 100Ah VRLA Batteries.
